name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
description: The incline dumbbell curl is performed lying on an incline bench set to approximately 45–60 degrees, with arms hanging behind the torso. This shoulder extension position places the long head of the biceps brachii under a greater stretch at the bottom of the movement, increasing its activation throughout the curl. The long head is particularly stimulated, contributing to the peak bicep appearance and the outer bicep fullness.

execution.starting_position: Set an adjustable bench to a 45–60 degree incline. Sit back against it with dumbbells in each hand, arms hanging straight down toward the floor. Palms face forward (supinated grip).
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust bench to between 45 and 60 degrees. Sit fully against the pad. The key is allowing the arms to hang behind the hip line for maximum bicep long head stretch.
steps: Step 1: Sit on the incline bench with arms hanging straight down behind the hips. Palms face forward.
Step 2: Begin from full arm extension — do not start with elbows bent.
Step 3: Exhale and curl both dumbbells upward simultaneously by flexing the elbows, keeping the upper arms stationary.
Step 4: Curl to full contraction, then inhale and lower slowly back to full arm extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the curl; inhale on the slow descent.
common_mistakes: Allowing the elbows to swing forward during the curl, reducing the long head stretch
Using too heavy a weight that shortens the range of motion
safety_considerations: The hanging arm position can stress the bicep tendon at the shoulder — start with lighter weight
Do not yank or jerk from the bottom position
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full hang at the bottom (arms fully extended); full curl at the top.
coaching_cues: Let the arms hang completely free behind you at the bottom — feel the long head stretching
Keep the elbows pinned back as you curl — do not let them drift forward
